digest.en: Trump threatens US tech firms with penalties for building datacenters abroad. Russia simultaneously rejects EU foreign policy chief Kallas in Ukraine talks, claiming her involvement would collapse negotiations.
digest.hi: पुतिन, ट्रंप और जिनपिंग की मुलाकात यूरोप को बाहर का रास्ता दिखा रही है। इसी बीच अमेरिकी वित्त मंत्री ने चीन को पुराने चिप्स बेचने पर नए प्रतिबंध लगाने से इनकार कर दिया।

articles.title: Trump threatens ‘tremendous penalties’ for US tech firms that build datacenters abroad
articles.summary: Donald Trump threatened to impose severe penalties on American tech firms constructing datacenters outside the United States. He made the statement during a White House press conference on Friday. The president provided no specific details regarding the nature or scale of these penalties. He also admitted he had not yet briefed his own officials on the plan. President gives wide-ranging White House press conference and says he has ‘fantastic relationships’ with Putin and XiDonald Trump threatened on Friday to impose “tremendous penalties” on American tech companies that build datacenters outside the US, though he gave no details and told reporters he had not yet informed his own officials about the plan. articles.title: Pakistan Army chief Munir vows to eliminate terrorism from country
articles.summary: Pakistan reported a sharp drop in terrorism during October. Attacks fell by 37 percent compared to September. Deaths from these incidents dropped by 57 percent. Injuries decreased by 71 percent, marking a significant decline in violence across the country. Pakistan overall witnessed a significant decline in terrorism-related violence during October, with attacks falling by 37%, deaths resulting from these attacks declining by 57%, and injuries decreasing by 71% compared to September, said Dawn newspaper report.

articles.title: U.S. sanctions Myanmar armed group leader over scam links
articles.summary: The U. S. Treasury froze assets of General Saw Shwe Wah. He leads the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army in Myanmar. The order bans Americans from dealing with him and a top officer. The move targets their links to scam operations. Treasury Department said on November 19 it had imposed an asset freeze on General Saw Shwe Wah, commander-in-chief of the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA), and one of his top officers, and had banned Americans from dealing with them.

articles.title: NIA sends request to UAE to probe any Indian footprints of copilot of flydubai flight who attacked
articles.summary: India's NIA requested UAE cooperation to probe a flydubai copilot. The officer attacked a passenger during a flight. Investigators seek to identify any Indian contacts in his circle. The NIA awaits documents and permission to join the investigation. “Who did the co-pilot come in contact with? Are there any Indian footprints of his friends circle who could be lurking. We will go ahead as soon as we get documents and permission from UAE to join the investigation,” says NIA chief.

articles.title: Pontoon Bridges, Hydrofoils, Tunnels: Barraged By Russia, Kyiv Rushes For Alternative River
articles.summary: Russia is targeting bridges spanning the Dnieper River in Kyiv. Ukrainian officials are developing alternatives to keep the city connected. Plans include pontoon bridges, hydrofoils, and tunnels. The goal is to prevent the capital from being cut in half. Russia is deliberately targeting the vital bridges that span the Dnieper River -- and link the two sides of Kyiv. Ukrainian officials are scrambling to come up with alternatives in case the city is completely cut in half.

articles.title: Russia says role for EU's Kallas in Ukraine talks with Moscow would lead to their collapse
articles.summary: Russia rejected EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas for Ukraine negotiations. Moscow's spokesperson called her unsuitable and anti-Russian. The Kremlin stated her involvement would cause talks to collapse immediately. Zakharova told a press briefing in Moscow that Kallas was totally unsuitable to take part in such talks and listed ‌a series of statements from Kallas which she ​said showed the EU official was anti-Russian.

articles.title: With Oil Revenue Running Out, Iran Teases Breaking US Blockade
articles.summary: Iranian hardliners are pushing for a tanker convoy to break the US naval blockade as oil revenue hits zero by mid-December. They threaten to strike Persian Gulf oil sites if the US fires on the vessels. This escalation risks a direct military confrontation in the region. With Iran’s oil revenue set to hit zero by mid-December, IRGC-linked media and hard-liners are pushing for a tanker convoy to break through the US naval blockade, threatening Persian Gulf oil sites if fired on.

articles.title: Xi’s new rulebook for local Party leaders
articles.summary: The Communist Party published new rules centralising control over local committees. The update sharpens the focus on Xi Jinping Thought and tightens personnel oversight. It also expands local committee authority and emphasises discipline. These changes mark a significant shift from the 2015 version. The Communist Party has published rules that centralise control over every provincial, city and county committee with four shifts from the 2015 version: a sharper focus on Xi Jinping Thought, a wider remit for local committees, tighter control over personnel and a new emphasis on discipline.

articles.title: General Assembly President tells Rohingya refugees after genocide ruling
articles.summary: The President of the United Nations General Assembly visited Cox’s Bazar in Bangladesh one day after the International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. The visit aimed to pressure the international community to translate the landmark legal finding into concrete protective measures. The court’s decision marks a significant shift in the diplomatic handling of the crisis. The President urged member states to move beyond rhetoric and implement the court’s directives.

articles.title: Record settler attacks mar olive harvest as UN urges Israel to protect farmers
articles.summary: Israeli settlers carried out over 400 attacks during this year’s West Bank olive harvest. This is the highest number recorded in any previous season. UN agencies and humanitarian groups urged Israel to protect farmers from the violence. The attacks caused casualties and significant property damage. Israeli settlers have carried out more than 400 attacks causing casualties or property damage during this year’s olive harvest in the occupied West Bank – more than in any previous season, UN agencies and humanitarian NGOs said on Friday.

articles.title: Shattered playgrounds and freezing classrooms: Inside Ukraine’s deadliest year for children
articles.summary: UNICEF highlighted record child casualty levels in Ukraine as the country faces another brutal winter. A twice-bombed Kyiv kindergarten stands in ruins during a day-long power cut. Freezing classrooms and shattered playgrounds illustrate the dangers children face. The conflict continues to inflict severe harm on the youngest population. Amid the ruins of a twice-bombed Kyiv kindergarten as a day-long power cut continued, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) on Friday highlighted the dangers to youngsters enduring another brutal winter in Ukraine, as child casualty numbers rise to record levels.

articles.title: Countries demand stronger climate deal as talks in Antalya reach final day
articles.summary: A coalition of countries challenged the proposed COP31 agreement, demanding explicit fossil fuel action. They also called for stronger climate finance commitments. Tensions rose as the Antalya summit neared its close. Negotiators struggled to find a deal acceptable to nearly 200 governments. A group of countries from Europe, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific has challenged the proposed COP31 agreement, demanding explicit action on fossil fuels and stronger climate finance.

articles.title: The secretive ICE force-feeding tactics that ended a Cuban father’s hunger strike
articles.summary: Cuban asylum seeker Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez ended a hunger strike in Texas. He described being force-fed through a tube after five days of resistance. The physical pain forced him to stop the protest. articles.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta subpoenaed Nvidia. The state investigates whether chip exports reached China despite restrictions. Officials suspect the company misled investors regarding compliance. State attorney says scandal ‘raises bright red flags’ and aims to find out if company misled investorsCalifornia has served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia after a scandal that prompted the departure of co-founder and longtime chief executive Jensen Huang. articles.title: China’s research ships turning ocean science into undersea warfare
articles.summary: China is expanding dual-use oceanographic ship deployments across the Indo-Pacific to map seafloors and track submarines. These vessels operate under scientific cover while threatening undersea cables. The strategy extends Beijing's military reach beyond traditional naval assets. Under the cover of scientific research and deep-sea exploration, China is deploying dual-use survey vessels across the Indo-Pacific to map seafloors, track submarines, and threaten undersea cables, bolstering its military reach.

articles.title: Shenzhen summit opens door to great power peace dialogue
articles.summary: US, Chinese, and Russian presidents met in Shenzhen to issue a joint peace declaration. The four-point document calls for United Nations reform, increased petroleum product supplies, and limits on international court jurisdiction. The leaders also committed to dialogue on reducing nuclear risks. The presidents of the United States, China and Russia have issued a four-point peace declaration calling for United Nations (UN) reform, more refined petroleum products, limits on the jurisdiction of international courts and dialogue on reducing nuclear risks.

articles.title: Battle to control GPS and radio signals raises civilian safety concerns
articles.summary: GPS and radio signals are increasingly blocked or faked, endangering aid convoys, passenger jets, and cargo ships. Civilian safety is declining as these critical navigation systems become unreliable. The disruption affects both conflict zones and open ocean routes. From aid convoys in conflict zones to passenger jets and cargo ships far out at sea, safe journeys depend on GPS, satellite navigation and old-fashioned radio transmissions.

articles.title: Ambition goes missing as fossil fuel language drops from draft deal
articles.summary: The latest draft climate agreement for COP31 removed explicit language on phasing out fossil fuels. This deletion occurred as ministers and the Presidency attempted to bridge sharp differences before the summit's scheduled close. Civil society groups expressed serious concern over the missing commitment. The change signals a significant retreat in the text's ambition regarding energy transition. A cat named Ambition went missing again at COP31 on Thursday.

articles.title: A Blown Bridge, A Big Meeting, And A 'Ludicrous Fantasy'
articles.summary: Moscow issued unrealistic European security demands despite losing the Kerch Bridge. The bridge partially collapsed during recent strikes. A meeting of three presidents drew attention. Analysts question the substance of the negotiations. Moscow makes what an analyst called "completely unrealistic" demands about European security despite setbacks in its war on Ukraine -- including the partial destruction of the only bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea.

articles.title: Iranian Doctor Accused Of Spreading 'False Information' About Single Mothers
articles.summary: Iranian authorities opened a case against an obstetrician for spreading false information. She posted a video noting a rise in single mothers. The action signals a crackdown on discussions of social change within the country. An Iranian obstetrician posted a video online in which she said she's observed a growing number of single women having babies. Iranian authorities reacted by opening a case against her for allegedly spreading misinformation, suggesting an effort to suppress discussions of social change.

articles.title: Ukraine Wrecked Putin's Bridge. Now It Can Choke Russian Supplies To Crimea
articles.summary: Ukraine destroyed the $4 billion Crimean Bridge, cutting road traffic between the Russian mainland and the peninsula. The damage severely strains Moscow's ability to supply the Black Sea region. Kyiv's strike targets a key Kremlin infrastructure asset. For eight years, it’s stood as a symbol of the Kremlin’s claim to Crimea: a $4 billion bridge directly linking the Russian mainland with the Ukrainian peninsula.

articles.title: RFE/RL Visits Ukraine's Newly Liberated Territory After Operation Vivaldi
articles.summary: Ukraine's Third Army Corps liberated 16 settlements and 277 square kilometers in Donetsk during Operation Vivaldi. RFE/RL journalists visited the newly secured frontline positions. They retraced the specific paths taken by Ukrainian infantry and assault troops during the military campaign. Ukraine's Third Army Corps liberated 16 settlements and 277 square kilometers in the Donetsk region during Operation Vivaldi. RFE/RL visits the frontline positions and retraces the path of the Ukrainian infantry and assault troops who took part in the military campaign.

articles.title: COP31 deadlock persists as countries launch new ‘climate reality check’
articles.summary: COP31 delegates in Antalya launched a new global check on climate promise fulfillment. Ministers remain deadlocked over funding responsibilities and fossil fuel transition timelines. The core dispute centers on whether a greener future is just if poorer nations cannot afford the shift. With the clock running down at COP31 in Antalya, countries on Wednesday launched a new global check on whether climate promises are being kept, even as ministers remained deadlocked over some of the summit’s toughest questions: who pays, how fast the world moves away from fossil fuels and whether a greener future can be called “just” if poorer countries cannot afford it.

articles.title: Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice is set to rule on Myanmar's genocide charges against the Rohingya. U. S. officials may sanction judges, including Nobel laureate Navi Pillay, if the ruling goes against the Myanmar government. articles.title: Diversifying funding was supposed to protect civil society: It did not
articles.summary: A survey of 195 organizations across 68 countries reveals that diversified funding strategies failed to protect civil society groups from the global aid retreat. The crisis extends beyond immediate financial shortfalls, indicating deeper structural vulnerabilities. Organizations that spent years building varied revenue streams are still facing severe operational challenges and instability. A survey of 195 organisations across more than 68 countries shows how the global aid retreat is hitting organizations that spent years building diverse funding streams.

articles.summary: अमृतपाल सिंह को अपनी दादी की अंत्येष्टि में शामिल होने के लिए दिल्ली लाया गया है। उन्हें 21 नवंबर को दोपहर 12 से तीन बजे के बीच का समय दिया गया है। सुरक्षा के कड़े इंतजाम किए गए हैं। अमृतपाल के पिता तरसेम सिंह ने बताया कि अमृतपाल सिंह की दादी का 8 नवंबर को निधन हो गया था। अमृतपाल को अंतिम संस्कार में शामिल होने के लिए 21 नवंबर को दोपहर 12 से तीन बजे के बीच का समय दिया गया है।
